title: Week 4 — Indicators of Sacred Law: Consensus (Ijmāʿ)

questions.q: Which definition of ijmāʿ matches the course material?
options: Agreement of all Muslims in any period on a social practice
Agreement of Muslim mujtahid-specialists after the Prophet’s death, during an era, on a sacred law ruling
Agreement of one school’s students on a legal question
A ruling inferred by analogy from a Qurʾānic verse

questions.q: Which example of ijmāʿ is specifically mentioned in the material?
options: The Companions’ agreement during ʿUthmān’s era to compile the Qurʾān into one codex
The agreement of all people to pray at the same time
A single jurist’s opinion on fasting
A later scholar’s preference for one interpretation

questions.q: The material identifies ijmāʿ as a valid indicator of sacred law rulings.
In general, the indication (dalālah) of ijmāʿ is described as:
Which of the following is listed as a possible basis (mustanad) of ijmāʿ?
options: A text from the Qurʾān or Sunnah
A personal preference with no legal basis
A modern custom alone, regardless of validity

questions.q: Some scholars restrict the basis of ijmāʿ to non-probabilistic indicators. Which examples do they accept according to the material?
options: Any opinion held by a majority

questions.q: Every mujtahid explicitly expresses agreement with a ruling, whether through fatwā or judgment. This is:
Some mujtahids state their position, while the remaining mujtahids know of it but remain silent without agreeing or disagreeing. This is:
The material says that the validity of silent/tacit unanimity is undisputed.
The mujtahids of an era express two or more different opinions, from which we infer that any opinion outside those positions is invalid. This is:
The material states that inferred unanimity (ijmāʿ ḍimnī) is debated as a valid indicator of sacred law rulings.
Which classification is correctly matched?
options: Ṣarīḥ — some scholars speak and the rest remain silent
Sukūtī — every mujtahid explicitly states agreement
Ḍimnī — agreement is inferred from the range of opinions expressed
Ḍimnī — one scholar issues a fatwā without any response

questions.q: What are the three types of ijmāʿ listed in the material?
acceptedAnswers: explicit, silent or tacit, and inferred

questions.q: What is the Arabic technical term for the basis on which consensus rests?
According to the definition in the material, whose agreement constitutes ijmāʿ?
options: Muslim mujtahid-specialists from the nation of Muḥammad ﷺ
The students of a single fiqh school
Only the rulers of an era

questions.q: According to the definition in the material, ijmāʿ refers to agreement reached after the Prophet’s death.
Which of the following is NOT listed as a basis of ijmāʿ in the material?
options: A text from the Qurʾān or Sunnah
Analogy based on a text from the Qurʾān or Sunnah
Another valid sacred law indicator, such as presumption of legal continuity
The personal preference of the majority without any indicator

questions.q: Which example does the material give of “other valid sacred law indicators” that may serve as a basis of ijmāʿ?
According to the material, some scholars do not accept probabilistic indicators, such as āḥād Sunnah and analogy, as a basis of ijmāʿ.
What is the indication (dalālah) of explicit unanimity (ijmāʿ ṣarīḥ) according to the material?
According to the material, explicit unanimity (ijmāʿ ṣarīḥ) may serve as a valid indicator of sacred law rulings.
Regarding silent unanimity (ijmāʿ sukūtī), the material states that:
options: Everyone agrees it is a valid and qaṭʿī indicator
It is debatable whether it is valid, and those who accept it debate whether its indication is probabilistic or non-probabilistic

questions.q: In silent unanimity, the mujtahids who remain silent are described as having:
options: Not known the opinion at all
Known the opinion but not expressed agreement or disagreement

questions.q: The mujtahids of an era split into two opinions on a case. What does inferred unanimity (ijmāʿ ḍimnī) conclude from this?
options: That they agree on the invalidity of any opinion outside those two
That the case has no ruling

questions.q: In explicit unanimity (ijmāʿ ṣarīḥ), what two forms may each mujtahid’s stated opinion take?
questions.displayAnswer: A fatwā (religious opinion) or a judgment (qaḍāʾ).
